text:
Dev Patel: Heads up — bench report launch week is coming up fast. Want to get Support readiness locked today: (1) expected inbound categories, (2) draft macros, (3) escalation owners + SLAs. Dropping a first pass below, pls reply w/ edits.

Dev Patel: Expected inbound buckets (from past launches + what Sales flagged):
1) “Can you share raw data / request logs?”
2) “Your region X numbers don’t match what I’m seeing.”
3) “How exactly is latency/$ computed?” (units, p50 vs p95, cost assumptions)
4) “Does caching/batching/quantization change the result?”
5) “Can I reproduce this with my prompts?”
6) “Security/privacy: did you use customer traffic? do you store prompts? data residency?”
7) “Pricing: does this imply my bill will be $Y?”
8) “Dedicated/Private: can you run this in our VPC / on-prem?”
9) Landing page issues: broken link, PDF won’t download, table not loading

Dev Patel: Draft escalation owners (proposed):
- Methodology/math questions -> Perf/Evals (Claire / Jonas) w/ Support-friendly blurb
- Region mismatch / suspected routing issue -> SRE on-call (Sean) + Routing (Mina/Ravi)
- Repro steps / SDK headers -> SE (Markus) or DX (Wei)
- Pricing interpretation / enterprise packaging -> Sales (Jordan/Stephanie/Lukas)
- Security/data handling -> Security/Compliance + existing FAQ (and Legal if claim-related)
- Web/PDF/table bug -> Docs/Web (Elliot)

Dev Patel: If you’re good with this split, I’ll bake into internal runbook + Zendesk macros.

SupportBot: Reminder: Please don’t paste customer prompts/logs into Slack. Use the “support-sensitive” doc if needed.

Jasmine Liu: +1. Also want a clear “when to escalate” threshold so L1 doesn’t ping Perf/Evals on every ticket. E.g. if it’s a generic “how did you measure?” -> macro + link. If they’re claiming “your numbers are wrong” or asking for deeper config differences -> escalate.

Ben Carter: Adding from Marketing side: we’re expecting a spike from the landing page CTA (“Talk to an engineer” + “Download PDF”). First 48h will be noisy. If Support gets “can you send me the PDF?” just point to the download link + ask them to try incognito if caching.

Wei Chen: For bucket (5) reproduce: we’ll have a public “how to reproduce” example + a docs section on region header selection. I can provide the canonical links and wording so Support doesn’t have to explain headers from memory.

Markus Klein: +1. Also anticipate “workload mismatch” tickets: ppl will say “my context length is 16k / my concurrency is 1” etc. We should have a short response: the benchmark uses a specific distribution; here’s how to adapt and what to expect.

Claire Dubois: Methodology escalation path works. Please make sure macro language doesn’t over-claim. We should consistently say “measured under the stated workloads/configs; expect variance; focus on relative comparisons within the same region/workload.” Also: we cannot share per-request raw logs. We can share the summarized table + confidence bands.

Sean Gallagher: For region mismatch: Support should collect a minimum set of info first (region, model, request type, streaming on/off, input/output token sizes, concurrency, time window, routing headers). Then escalate to SRE. Otherwise we just play 20 questions.

Dev Patel: Great. I’ll draft macros now. Please comment inline (or reply) with any must-have fields.

Dev Patel: Macro v0 — “Raw data / logs request”
---
Thanks for reaching out. We can’t share raw per-request logs or any customer-identifying telemetry.

What we can share:
• The published report + methodology appendix
• The public benchmark tables (sanitized and aggregated)
• Guidance on how to reproduce a scaled version of the benchmark against your own workload

Links:
- Report PDF: <https://redwood.example/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar#download>
- Methodology: <https://redwood.example/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar#methodology>
- Reproduce example: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/tree/main/reproduce-benchmark>

If you tell us your target region(s), model family, and typical context/output sizes, we can point you to the closest benchmark slice.
---

Jasmine Liu: Add 1 line that we intentionally avoid publishing anything that could let people infer fleet internals / per-request traces. (Some security buyers ask that.)

Dev Patel: Noted.

Dev Patel: Macro v0 — “Region mismatch vs report”
---
Thanks — differences can happen due to region selection, routing/fallback behavior, workload shape (token sizes, concurrency), and time-of-day conditions.

To help us compare apples-to-apples, can you share:
1) Which region you’re targeting (and whether you set a region header)
2) Model name + version (if pinned)
3) Request type (chat vs embeddings), streaming on/off
4) Typical input/output tokens (rough ranges are fine)
5) Concurrency / QPS and whether you’re batching client-side
6) Timestamp window + your measured p50/p95 latency

In parallel, here are the exact benchmark conditions used in the report (workload distribution + measurement window):
<https://redwood.example/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar#methodology>

Once we have the details above, we can advise reproduction steps and escalate to our SRE/perf team if something looks off.
---

Sean Gallagher: Please add: “If you did not set a region header, you may be served by smart routing depending on your account settings.” And include link to region header docs.

Wei Chen: Here’s the region header doc link we want Support to use: <https://docs.redwood.example/api/regions#selecting-a-region> (also mentions OpenAI-compat header variant). 

Dev Patel: Perfect.

Dev Patel: Macro v0 — “How is latency/$ computed?”
---
In the report, “latency per dollar (latency/$)” is a derived metric combining:
• A latency statistic from the benchmark runs (reported as p50 and p95)
• The measured effective cost for the run (from metered token throughput under the benchmark configuration)

It’s intended to help compare production economics under a fixed workload definition. It’s not a guarantee of what any single application will see.

Details (including workload definition, warmup, caching policy, and how cost is calculated) are in the methodology appendix:
<https://redwood.example/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar#methodology>

If you share your workload shape (region, tokens, concurrency), we can help map you to the closest benchmark slice and suggest how to reproduce.
---

Claire Dubois: Suggest adding: “We report confidence/variance bands across repeated runs; small differences are often within run-to-run variance.”

Dev Patel: Will add.

Markus Klein: Also add “p50 is median request latency; p95 is tail latency.” People ask.

Dev Patel: Yep.

Dev Patel: Macro v0 — “Caching/batching/quantization questions”
---
The benchmark uses a published configuration (including batching/caching policy) to reflect a realistic production setup. Changing batching, caching, quantization profile, or context length distribution can change both latency and cost.

If you tell us what knobs you’re considering (e.g., continuous batching level, prefix caching on/off, quant profile), we can recommend a setup and help you run a reproduction test.

Methodology/config: <https://redwood.example/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar#methodology>
Reproduce guide: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/tree/main/reproduce-benchmark>
---

Ben Carter: From GTM perspective we should keep this macro neutral. Don’t imply “turn on X and you’ll match the chart.” Just say “these knobs affect results; here’s what we used.”

Dev Patel: Agreed.

Dev Patel: Macro v0 — “Security / data handling”
---
We did not use or disclose any customer-identifying request logs in the public report. Results are based on controlled benchmark workloads run in dedicated benchmark windows.

We publish aggregated metrics (e.g., latency percentiles, throughput, derived cost metrics) and a methodology appendix; we do not publish raw request traces.

Security & data handling FAQ:
<https://redwood.example/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar#security>

If you have specific requirements (SSO, audit logs, retention controls, data residency), tell us what you need and we’ll connect you with the right team.
---

Jasmine Liu: Add a line for EU prospects: “We report results by region and you can select region for residency needs.” (But careful: don’t overpromise about residency without the standard disclaimer.)

Wei Chen: I can supply the standard wording we use in docs: “Region selection controls where inference is served; customers are responsible for configuring region selection consistent with their requirements.”

Dev Patel: Great, send it.

Dev Patel: Ops/process proposal for launch week (Mon-Fri):
- L1 Support uses macros + collects info. 
- If escalation needed, tag as:
  * “BENCH-METHODOLOGY” -> Perf/Evals (Claire) response target: same business day
  * “BENCH-REGION-MISMATCH” -> SRE (Sean) initial triage: 4h business hours
  * “BENCH-DOCS” -> Wei/Elliot: 1 business day
  * “BENCH-PRICING/SALES” -> Jordan/AE owner: same day handoff
- If anything looks like an incident (site down, API errors, elevated latency), open #eng-sre + incident process. 

Sean Gallagher: +1 but define “incident-like”: multiple tickets in <30 min for same symptom OR we see correlated graphs. Support can post in #eng-sre with “FYI, not declaring incident yet” so we can watch.

Owen Phillips: For BENCH-REGION-MISMATCH, if we suspect perf regression vs baseline: route to me as Tier-3 once SRE confirms it’s not general region health. I can compare traces + runtime flags used during bench windows.

Dev Patel: Sounds good.

Ben Carter: Where should Support point people asking “can you run this for my workload” (custom benchmark request)? We’re trying to route those to “book a consult.”

Markus Klein: For enterprise-ish: route to SE via AE; for self-serve: we can point to reproduce example and offer office hours. I’d prefer Support not commit to “we’ll run it for you” unless Sales/SE approves.

Jasmine Liu: +1. We can also offer: “share a small prompt set + expected QPS and we’ll advise which config/model family to test.” But keep it bounded.

Dev Patel: I’ll add a macro snippet: “We can’t run bespoke benchmarks for every workload via Support; please use the reproduce guide or book a consult.”

Wei Chen: One more: anticipate “PDF says APAC includes X, but I can’t select that region.” That’s usually account allowlist / rollout. Support should collect org ID + desired region, then escalate to Product/Support ops.

Dev Patel: Good catch.

Dev Patel: Action items:
- Dev: finalize macros + put in Zendesk + internal doc
- Wei: send canonical links + EU residency phrasing
- Sean: send minimum info checklist + what counts as incident-ish
- Claire: provide 3–5 sentences “methodology blurb” Support can paste w/o edits
- Ben: confirm final landing page URLs + download link so we don’t paste drafts

Ben Carter: Confirmed URLs will be stable by EOD. I’ll drop them here once PR merges.

Claire Dubois: Methodology blurb draft (Support-safe):
“We ran repeated benchmark suites using a published workload definition (request types, token size distributions, and concurrency) and reported both median (p50) and tail (p95) latency along with variance across runs. ‘Latency per dollar’ is a derived metric combining observed latency with measured cost under the benchmark configuration. These results are intended for like-for-like comparisons under the stated conditions; your application may differ based on workload shape, region selection, and configuration.”

Dev Patel: This is perfect. :thumbsup:

Sean Gallagher: Minimum info checklist for region mismatch / perf tickets:
- org ID
- region header (yes/no + value)
- model + version
- endpoint type (chat/embeddings)
- streaming (yes/no)
- input/output token approx
- concurrency/QPS
- timeframe
- client location (rough geo)
- whether retries/timeouts enabled client-side

Dev Patel: Great. I’m going to compile all of this into the launch-week support runbook and post in #support-announcements.

Jasmine Liu: Can we also prep 1 internal note for Support: “If asked who ‘Redwood’ is benchmarking against, do not speculate; only speak to what’s in report.” (We’ve had folks get baited.)

Ben Carter: Yes — that’s in claims guidelines. Support should redirect to methodology + not do competitor-by-competitor debates in tickets.

Dev Patel: Adding that as a do/don’t at the top. Thanks all.
